answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. The practical consequence is a steady economy where reputation is earned slowly, spent carefully, and never inflated by a sudden influx of cheap accounts. Consider a violet as the anchor of the cost. A ivory stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a wharf...
